mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) above 2% year-over-year indicates inflationary pressure, leading to tighter monetary policy expectations and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite negative signal.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% in one month signals economic weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in > 50% of triggered instances despite negative signal.

mechanism_narrative: A significant drop in housing starts (HOUST) indicates a weakening demand in the housing market, which is a leading indicator of broader economic slowdown and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite negative signal.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) signals strengthening economic activity, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is above 6% and the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is below 1%, it indicates a loose monetary policy in a weak labor market, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
regime_hint: loose monetary policy in weak labor market
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite positive signal.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) by more than 2% month-over-month signals a contraction in consumer spending, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite negative signal.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is rising and the GDP (GDPC1) growth is slowing, it indicates a tightening monetary policy in a slowing economy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rising and GDPC1 growth slowing
regime_hint: tightening monetary policy in slowing economy
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite negative signal.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) by more than 200,000 in a month signals strong labor market conditions, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite positive signal.
